title: Session Playback: Correlated Trace Session Inspector
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an inspector view for the Redwood Console that allows engineers to play back a single user request session across correlated traces. The inspector should group spans by correlation IDs, show a compact synchronized timeline + scrubber, surface linked logs and metrics, and provide filters for latency buckets, error state, and sampled vs unsampled requests. Goals: reduce time-to-root-cause by enabling a single-click pivot from dashboard anomaly to full session context; make the interaction performant for sessions with thousands of spans; preserve keyboard navigation and accessibility for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Deep-linkable inspector URL that opens to a single trace session (supporting correlation_id param)
Timeline scrubber with zoom levels (overview, per-span, microsecond level) and smooth pan/zoom on large sessions
Span groupings by correlation_id with toggle for showing raw span tree
Filter panel that supports boolean rules, latency bucket quick-sets (p95+, p99+, >500ms), and tag search
Linked logs and metric sparklines visible inline for focused span; clicking a log opens log viewer pane
Prototype validated with at least 3 engineers and 1 SRE in usability testing and no major blocking issues
Design assets (Figma) and handoff tokens submitted to frontend with CSS/interaction spec
comments: 2026-02-28 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created with early wireframes. Focus on grouping spans by correlation ID rather than flattening every span into a single timeline; avoids overwhelming users for high-throughput requests.

2026-03-01 Luca Romero: Added key interactions — scrub to nearest span, snap-to-error, keyboard shortcut 'f' to toggle filter panel. Raised question about handling sessions with >20k spans; recommended aggregation / sampling visualization.

2026-03-02 Priya Patel (SRE): Reviewed prototype — asked for integration points with logs (link by trace_id and time offset) and suggested showing upstream/downstream service latency deltas. Also flagged need for guardrails when loading huge sessions to avoid OOM in browser.

2026-03-03 Jon Alvarez (Frontend): Implementation note — will expose a paginated span loader and use canvas-based rendering for timeline to keep CPU low. Needs final spec on hover states and focus management.

2026-03-03 Design Review: Team demoed prototype in design review. Feedback: improve affordance for sampling indicator, make latency buckets configurable, and add copy-to-clipboard on deep-link. Approved to hand off with minor changes.
decisions: Use correlation_id as primary pivot: UI groups spans by correlation_id and offers expand/collapse to reveal full span tree per correlation group.
Render timeline using canvas + virtualized DOM for span list to support very large sessions without blocking repaints.
Provide two default latency buckets (p95+, p99+) and allow users to add custom thresholds in preferences.
Sampling indicator: show a colored badge (green/yellow/red) with tooltip explaining sampling rate and whether this session is complete or partial
next_steps: Finalize hover/focus interaction spec and hand off to ENG-4678 (frontend) for initial spike
Coordinate with backend ENG-4520 to add correlation_id param to trace export API and streaming endpoint
Run 3 moderated usability sessions (SREs, backend eng, product) and incorporate feedback into final prototype
Create QA checklist for performance testing with synthetic sessions of 1k, 10k, and 50k spans
qa_notes: Focus on rendering performance (time-to-first-paint < 1s for 1k spans), memory usage in Chromium, keyboard navigation, and correctness of deep-link params. Test on macOS Safari, Chrome, and Windows Edge.
